prerequisites: Mathematics basics from analysis and applied algebra courses

learning_outcomes.text: Upon completion of this course, the student is able to apply techniques of probability, statistics, and data analysis in engineering practice.
The student learns to choose appropriate models and calculation methods, estimate parameters, assess uncertainties, and perform correct data analyses.
Emphasis is placed on insight, practical knowledge of calculation rules and methods, and applications to example datasets from engineering applications.

syllabus_topics: Random experiments, outcomes, the universe and events
Probability of the complement and the union
Probability distribution of a random variable
Probability distributions derived from the Bernoulli experiment
Overview of other probability distributions + examples
Probability distribution of a random vector
Conditional expected values and sequential calculation
Regression lines of a bivariate probability distribution
Estimating confidence intervals using parametric method
Estimating confidence intervals using non-parametric method (+ bootstrapping)
Structure and construction of statistical hypothesis
Relationship between confidence intervals and hypothesis testing

Exercise sessions on PC: solving problems with given datasets, with applications from various engineering disciplines; additional datasets are provided for independent practice in preparation for the exam
Interpreting results of exploratory data analysis and performing simple probability calculations
Choosing probability models and calculating probabilities
Estimating parameters of probability models, constructing confidence intervals
DATA SCIENCE, PREDICTIVE MODELS AND UNCERTAINTIES
Validation of regression models with residual analysis
Types of uncertainties in modeling: model-input, -parameter, -model structure uncertainties
as a bridge between statistics and machine learning
Concepts of statistical learning, data mining, inference, prediction, …

Exercise sessions on PC: solving problems with given datasets, with applications from various engineering disciplines; additional datasets are provided for independent practice in preparation for the exam.
Data-based learning: algorithm for machine learning, supervised versus unsupervised learning, regularization

assessment_methods.method: Written exam during the examination period

institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
